item.title: Reddit is killing RSS feeds and ending public API access because of AI bots
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Reddit is ending support for RSS feeds, as the company continues tightening access to its trove of user-generated content.

item.title: The ugly economics of consumer AI
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: There’s a reason frontier labs have gotten gunshy about consumer AI — and it’s not because the tech isn’t good enough.

item.title: Meta disputes claim that Muse read a user’s private messages without permission
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Meta says its Muse AI agent cannot access a user’s Messages without explicit permission, disputing a journalist’s account that the agent read his private messages while the required Mac setting was turned off.

item.title: DoorDash launches an AI agent you can text to order food
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: By launching an AI agent for food ordering, DoorDash is looking to gain an edge over rivals Uber Eats and Grubhub.

item.title: Destro AI’s secret sauce is getting robots and humans on the same page
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: "One of the biggest reasons we are winning against robotics companies is because we are not a robotics company."

item.title: Instinct’s new product recommendations are giving some users the ick
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Instinct is rolling out human-curated product and travel recommendations, but some users aren’t happy about getting suggestions they never asked for.

item.title: FedEx orders 2,000 electric trucks from Harbinger in $300M deal
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The order -- Harbinger's biggest ever -- comes as the startup is reportedly considering an IPO.

item.title: Pledge signed by President Trump and top AI leaders misspells the United States
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: On Tuesday, President Donald Trump and top AI leaders announced a signed pledge called a “Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities” — a voluntary promise to implement more controls and safety measures as the rapid development of artificial intelligence continues. But there seems to be a catch.

item.title: Google launches Fitbit Air in India, though its high price might deter the masses
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Fitbit Air costs around $146 in India, roughly $47 more than its U.S. pricing.

item.title: Instagram rolls out an AI video assistant for creators
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: This conversational AI assistant is intended to provide personalized feedback to creators, rather than generic advice.

item.title: Cerebras Systems’ Andrew Feldman on whether AI can keep scaling at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman will explore the growing demand for compute, energy, and infrastructure, how Cerebras is approaching those constraints differently, and what comes next if today’s AI hardware reaches its limits.

item.title: Restate lands $20M as the need for durable infrastructure increases with AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Instead of building its durable execution engine on top of an external database, the company developed its own storage, replication, and redundancy layers. This architecture allows Restate to be exceptionally fast and lightweight.

item.title: 3 days left to exhibit: Turn visibility into your next opportunity at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Three days left to exhibit at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Book by October 2 at 11:59 p.m. PT to showcase your startup to 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders.

item.title: WhatsApp adds new parental controls for teen accounts
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Parents can limit how teens use channels, whose Status they can see, who can see their Status updates, and control who can add teens to groups.

item.title: Amazon’s new Fire TV Stick 4K comes with an actually good remote
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Amazon’s new Fire TV Stick 4K is slimmer and faster, but its biggest upgrade may be the thing you’ll actually hold in your hand: a redesigned remote that’s easier to use, especially in the dark.

item.title: Charter Space raises $5M to bring insurance to the stars
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: As Charter explains on its website, a common experience for space companies is that regular insurers "heard a bunch of scary science words and freaked out."

item.title: Tinder adapts to a social, IRL dating future with ‘Group Hangouts’ feature
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Tinder has been pushing users toward more real-world experiences for some time.

item.title: Two Google alumni raise $11.3M to back AI startups that enterprises will actually pay for
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: BAG Ventures announces close of a $11.3M Fund I to invest in all things AI.

item.title: Airbnb adds AI search, more social features
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Airbnb is also launching new services such as meal delivery and laundry in select locations.

item.title: Apple Pay finally launches in India after years on the sidelines
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Some of India's largest banks are holding off on supporting Apple Pay initially.
